To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) Ena1 is expressed in a pH-dependent manner, (ii) the pH response of Ena1 expression is mediated by the calcineurin pathway through two binding sites in the ENa1 promoter and (iii) a second input, likely mediated by Snf1, also contributes to this response.

1) the Ena1 response to alkalinisation is mediated by two stress-responsive Crzl binding sites in the ENa1 promoter, 2) Crz1 is the main transcription factor responsible for the initial induction of Ena1 expression in response to alkaline pH stress, and 3) the initial induction of ENA1 expression in response alkaline pH is mediated by the calcineurin-Crz1 pathway and the Snf1 pathway.

1) the Ena1 expression is regulated by calcineurin/Czr1 under high pH stress; 2) this regulation is achieved by two Crz1-binding motifs in the promoter of the ENA gene; 3) Crz1 is the main contributor to the early response, but other transcription factors are likely to participate; and 4) the response to pH stress is likely to be mediated by a second signaling pathway, in addition to calcineurin,
In summary, our research is concerned with
a detailed analysis of the regulation of Ena1 expression under alkaline pH stress.
the quantitative analysis of the response of the Ena ATPase to high pH stress and the role of calcineurin/Crzi in this response.
a quantitative analysis of the regulation of the Na+-ATPases in the budding yeast.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the response of the ENa1 promoter to high pH is regulated by two different pathways, one mediated by calcineurin/Crzi and the other by Snf1.
the ENA1 gene is regulated in a complex way by at least two inputs: one mediated by the calcineurin-Crz1 pathway and another one mediated by Snf1.
Crz1 is the major regulator of the Ena Na+ pump under high pH stress, and it contributes to the initial response of the Ena pump to high salt stress.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the ENA1 gene responds to alkalinization by a complex regulatory mechanism, in which the calcineurin/Czr1 system is the major contributor, but not the unique one, to the early transcriptional response.
the expression of the Enal Na+-ATPases is regulated by two different signaling pathways, one mediated by calcineurin/Crxl and the other by Snf1.
the response of Ena1 expression to high pH stress is mediated by two inputs: the calcineurin pathway and a second input that is likely mediated by the Snf1/Snf4 complex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quantitative analysis of gene expression data in combination with mathematical modeling can provide valuable information about the molecular mechanisms involved in gene expression regulation.
the quantitative study of the response of the yeast ENA1 promoter to environmental stimuli can be successfully performed using a mathematical modeling approach.

the response of ENA1 to alkalinization can be explained in quantitative terms, with a clear role for Crz1, and that the models developed here can provide a framework for further studies on the regulation of the ENA ATPase by calcineurin.
